**ServiceNow, Inc. (CIK 1373715) — debt profile as of December 31, 2024**

**Bottom line:** ServiceNow carries very little debt relative to its size and liquidity. Its capital structure is essentially one bond issue plus a large investment portfolio, so the company is a net holder of financial assets rather than a leveraged borrower.

**Structure — a single, long-dated, fixed-rate unsecured bond**
- In August 2020 the company issued **1.40% fixed-rate ten-year senior notes with $1.5 billion aggregate principal, due September 1, 2030** (the "2030 Notes"). They were issued at 99.63% of principal, with about $13 million of debt issuance costs; the effective interest rate was **1.53%**. Interest is paid semi-annually (March 1 and September 1), and the entire principal is due at maturity. The notes are **unsecured**, with customary covenants that restrict liens on specified assets and sale-leaseback transactions (2024 Form 10-K, Note 11 "Debt"; also MD&A "Market Risk").
- **Carrying value:** $1,489 million at 12/31/2024 and $1,488 million at 12/31/2023, net of unamortized discount and issuance costs of $11 million and $12 million respectively (Note 11).
